cost: A PIN WAS RELEASED BY TOMER, NOT BY THE AGENT. recal_89's Chauncey Billups '06 off 86 +-1 is moved to data/anchors_superseded.json with the reason 'released by Tomer on round 154 (Push 154-157): the hub floor ramp pays the volume-60-to-68 creation class', and he is re-pinned at off 91 +-1 (round 154). The previous, DECLINED 154 proved over the whole family that no ramp monotone in volume can separate Billups (volume 66, playvol 88, efficiency 92) from the subject (65, 91, 76): the last ramp foot Billups survives, 65.5, pays the subject exactly zero. So the round could only land once he chose the level, and he did.

TWO NEW ANCHORS: Chauncey Billups '06 off 91 +-1 (round 154) and Kevin Johnson '92 off 81 +-3 (round 154). The subject reads 80, which is inside the tolerance; the pin stays at 81 +-3 rather than being moved down to the reached value, because 81 is the number the ruling names. 151 anchors, 0 failing, mean |error| 0.79.

THE FOOTPRINT: 228 of 10,000 cards move on OFF, EVERY ONE OF THEM UP, mean +1.83, max +6; 184 OVRs follow; DEF and every attribute move on ZERO; every mover has volume between 49 and 67, which is the ramp's window and nothing else. OFF_TOP and DEF_TOP are NOT re-derived, so no card above the knee moves and recal_90's warning does not apply to this round. data/build_ratings.py is untouched — the attributes are not in dispute.

THE DEVIATION TAX LAW COST THREE CONSTANTS. The 228 risers are guards and wings in the harness's ovr>=55 pool, so the fives it draws got better at offence and all three taxes whose benefit reads an offensive mismatch fell out of band AT ONCE — hunt on the ORACLE edge (+0.4165 at 4.05) and crash off / crash def on the BLIND edge (-0.2014 at .17, -0.0094 at .48), the two edges in opposite directions in the same round for the first time. Each was swept ONCE from main's constant and set at its true midpoint by recal_126's rule: hunt 4.05 -> 3.67 (feasible 3.510-3.834), crashOff 0.17 -> 0.70 (feasible .327-1.067), crashDef 0.48 -> 0.98 (feasible .858-1.101). All nine rows pass. Hunt's thirteenth move, and it walks back down the jump recal_151 made it take.

TEAM DIALS: three adjacent swaps in the all-time franchise-fives tier, no dial value changed on any other level. All-time Pistons and Knicks trade rounds 4 and 5 (Billups '06 is the Piston), Trail Blazers and Nuggets trade 7 and 8, Raptors and Bucks trade 14 and 15. notes: WHAT THE RULING WAS REALLY ABOUT, in one term. The subject's o_score before: the hub channel paid him 0.000 and his signature term read 3.95 on a volume floor of 50. recal_138 gave the hub class TWO tests — a creation SURPLUS (playvol - volume, deliberately ramped 'so it is a fade and not a step') and a volume FLOOR (volume >= 68, left as a step). Kevin Johnson '92 passes the first at 0.85 and failed the second by three points of volume. After the round his role reads 0.85 x 0.85 = 0.7225, the premium is +3.867 and the signature floor lifts to 58.79: o_score 81.12 -> 85.82, OFF 75 -> 80.

WHY A RAMP AND NOT A LOWER STEP. A lower step moves the cliff, it does not remove it; the previous 154 measured the cliff's width at 5 printed OFF points for a guard at flat minutes, which is the same size wherever it is put. The ramp is the form recal_138 already chose for the OTHER half of the same class function and it reuses that half's width (HUB_FULL - HUB_GATE = 20), so the round introduces no constant and invents no shape. recal_138's own COST named this seam (Nash '03 vs '05) as OPEN rather than accepted.

THE DISJOINTNESS CLAIM IS NOT WEAKENED, IT IS MADE CONTINUOUS. recal_117's elite-passer gate ramps to exactly zero going UP at volume 68; the hub now ramps to exactly zero going DOWN at 48. Between 48 and 68 both channels pay a fraction, and the fractions sum to less than either channel alone would pay at full size — the same overlap construction recal_112/109 use across playvol 70. No card is paid twice for one assist rate at any volume, which is the property recal_138's block claims and which the step was only one way of getting.
EVERY BIG IS BYTE-IDENTICAL. `is_big(p)` short-circuits the whole expression and returns role 1.00, exactly as recal_55 wrote it, so no centre reads the volume ramp at all. Measured: 0 bigs moved.

THE SUBJECT LANDS AT 80 AGAINST A TARGET OF 81. That is inside the orchestrator's 81 +-3 and it is the honest reading of the form, not a value tuned to the number: the ramp's shape was fixed by the constants already in the file before the subject was read. Nothing in the round is a per-player override; the change is a class function evaluated on every perimeter card in the pool.
